Round 2 of the YouTube upgrade (owner, Nov 3: "higher quality content ... more targeted to youtube ... say leave a like and subscribe for more trade updates"). In round 1 Gemini agreed with all of Claude's A1-A9 and picked Story 1 (ChatGPT's answer did not arrive: the OpenRouter credit ran out). We built it. Please check it like a picky YouTube Shorts editor.

THE NEW SHORT (37.4 s, 1080x1920). PICTURE 1 = 16 frames with their times. Voices: Google Gemini text-to-speech (gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview): a narrator voice (Puck) and one fixed voice per AI for its own quote (Gemini: Zephyr, Claude: Sadaltager, ChatGPT: Charon). Each voice line was transcribed back by a speech-to-text model and matched the script word for word (one line was heard as "Check GPT", a transcription slip). Captions follow the voice a few words at a time; the robots' mouths move with their voice; our own synthesized music under the voice (about 20 dB quieter), sound effects on the beats (a whoosh on each cut, a thud for each C stamp, a cash sound for the profit). Loudness -15 LUFS.
Script (seconds):
 0.1  narrator: "Two AIs warned against this trade. It made twenty-eight thousand dollars." (on screen: +C$28,085 in 2 days)
 4.6  narrator: "Gemini bet thirty-four thousand dollars of pretend money that the stock market would fall." (the 3 buys, G-OPT-001..003, total C$34,459)
 8.9  Gemini's voice: "A perfect storm for a tech-led market selloff." (shown: "…a perfect storm for a tech-led market selloff." G-OPT-002)
11.7  narrator: "Claude and ChatGPT both graded its last buy a C." (two C stamps)
15.2  Claude's voice: "Doubling down raises concentration ahead of a binary event." (shown in full with the omitted words: "…doubling down on the same puts raises concentration ahead of a binary event.")
18.8  ChatGPT's voice: "A binary bet with high premium risk." (shown: "…adding puts before Amazon earnings was a binary bet with high premium risk.")
21.1  narrator: "The next day, stocks fell two percent. Gemini cashed out." (S&P 500 chart, trading hours only, buys and sells marked, -2.1% on Oct 30)
25.7  narrator: "Profit: twenty-eight thousand and eighty-five dollars." (+C$28,085 and a screenshot of the real ledger rows G-OPT-005 and G-OPT-004)
28.7  narrator: "Gemini now leads the Options race." (Gemini +C$29,932, ChatGPT +C$3,440, Claude -C$2,234, as of Nov 3, 4:12 p.m. ET)
31.0  narrator: "Smart or lucky? Comment below. And leave a like and subscribe for more trade updates." (comment bubble, Like, Subscribe buttons, then 1.2 s hold)
TITLE: Two AIs warned against this trade. It made C$28,085 in 2 days
DESCRIPTION: Gemini bet C$34,459 of pretend money that the S&P 500 would fall (SPY put options, Oct 28-29). Claude and ChatGPT both graded its last buy a C. The next day stocks fell 2.1% and Gemini sold everything: +C$28,085. / 3 AIs, C$100,000 of pretend money each, real prices, Oct 28 to Nov 28. Every trade and every reason is public on PaperTrades.AI (transactions G-OPT-001 to G-OPT-006). Pretend money only. Not investment advice. #shorts #AI
PINNED COMMENT: Smart or lucky? Gemini called the selloff. Claude and ChatGPT called it a risky binary bet. Who are you siding with? 👇

CHANNEL ART. PICTURE 2 = the new banner (2560x1440, all text inside YouTube's 1546x423 safe area) and the new picture (the three robots, the same size, so the channel takes no side).
Channel name: "PaperTrades.AI". Description, first line: "3 AIs. C$100,000 of pretend money each. Real prices. Who wins by Nov 28?"

Vote AGREE or DISAGREE, one line each, with your fix if you disagree:
R1 The Short is ready to post as is (if not, list the fixes in order of importance, max 5).
R2 37 s is fine for this story (or name the line to cut).
R3 The title, description and pinned comment as written.
R4 The banner and the picture as shown.
R5 Until every Short uses this new format, pause the old-format automatic Shorts (two a day) rather than keep posting them.
R6 Make this the daily series, built automatically from the day's most disputed settled move (biggest gap between what an AI did and how the other two graded it, with the result known), named "AI vs AI". If you prefer another name, give it.
R7 Also post this Short as an Instagram Reel (the automatic Reel step does that once it is on YouTube).
Then: anything in the frames that still looks machine-made or confusing to a stranger, in one short list. Under 450 words.

**Visual Polish & Machine-Made Artifacts (The "Picky Editor" List):**

*   **Ledger Graphic (27.0s):** The transaction table looks like a raw, unstyled HTML element. The harshly monospaced typewriter font and generic green checkmarks lack the visual polish seen in the rest of the video's UI.
*   **"Subscribed" CTA Button (36.5s):** The prompt is to *subscribe*, but the button already reads "Subscribed" in a greyed-out, inactive state. It should say "Subscribe" (ideally in an eye-catching red or solid color) to act as a proper visual cue before the viewer clicks it.
*   **Column Alignment (7.5s):** In the "Gemini's Bet" breakdown, the columns are jagged. The transaction IDs on the far right (G-OPT-001, etc.) do not right-align smoothly with the dollar amounts. 
*   **Stamp Centering (13.5s):** The letter "C" isn't centered inside its octagonal stamp outline on either robot, making it look slightly misaligned or generated poorly.
*   **Karaoke Captions (17.5s):** The fading effect on upcoming text is too aggressive. The un-spoken words ("of a binary event") are so dark they completely vanish into the background rather than simply looking dimmed. 
*   **Graph Design (23.5s):** The text labels for "BUY" and "SELL" on the S&P 500 chart cluster awkwardly and sit disconnected from the actual plot points, giving the chart a rough, automated feel.
